sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sarras was an Arthurian site. This city was the source of the Grail and the destination of the knights who sought that sacred object. The name appears to come from the term Saracens, used in the medieval period for eastern Mediterranean or Islamic warriors. Some sources claim that Sarras was the place of Galahad's death. The city belongs to the Grail quest literature. It is a legendary place rather than a real city, and its geography comes from romance rather than record. The Grail reached its keeper only after the true knight completed the quest. This made Sarras the endpoint of the search and the resting place of a holy prize.
